## INIT2 · INIT2-con-id — d3: consoled cannot see a connection's id

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 8

Evidence: Ruled (a) three times and built on wp-init2: the skeleton passes a minted connection's id to FileServer::minted (9974c7e5f, host test the_file_server_learns_the_id_the_requester_got); consoled prefixes [con N] with N the 16-hex-digit id and init announces in the same format, and the check refuses a handed item at consoled's endpoint so only init holds a root badge there (b87c9d086, init-refuses-consoled-handed); consoled's per-bucket state is MAX_THREADS by name, BUDGET computed at 31 and 255 (8ba51011f, host test init_s_badge_mints_a_console_for_every_server_init_can_start). Page lines on consoled.md and testbench.md; the Architect checks them at INIT2's review.

Event: `54146033a78092636c5ba14e8b98183f` · 2026-10-03T01:55:55Z

> d3 gap (blocking for d3 only; I go on with d4's refusal cases meanwhile).
> 
> consoled.md "Started by init": a write through a minted connection starts each line with `[con N] `, N = that connection's id, the id init prints bare. That id is the random id Minted draws in `reserve` (libs/rt/src/server/minted.rs, `Ticket.id`/`Entry.id`, private) and returns to the requester. consoled's FileServer::write sees only `Caller.badge`; the skeleton's `minted(caller, badge, root, quota)` hook gets no id. So consoled cannot map badge -> id without a change in libs/rt/src/server/{minted,ninep}.rs, which the brief does not give INIT2 (owned: admit.rs only).
> 
> Options:
> (a) [recommended] rt: `Ticket::id()` getter, and the skeleton passes the id to the file server: add `id: u64` to `FileServer::minted` (3 other impls: ipd fs.rs, ninep_tests.rs, libs/client tests common — each just takes `_id`). consoled records badge->id there and forgets it in `disconnected`. ~10 lines in rt plus a skeleton host test that the hook gets the id the requester got.
> (b) Same, but a new default hook `fn named(&mut self, badge, id) {}` called after commit: no impl churn, but two hooks for one event and a window where minted() accepted a badge with no id yet.
> (c) No rt change: N is the badge, not the id. init does not learn the badge from new_connection ((Endpoint, id) only), so the announce line could not carry it: contradicts the page and ruling 6. Not viable without changing new_connection's reply.
> 
> Also, ruling 6 asks me to fix one format: I propose N as the id in 16 lowercase hex digits, zero-padded (`[con 0f3a…]`, announce `init: started NAME, console 0f3a…`), stated on consoled.md and testbench.md. Say if you prefer decimal (init prints decimal today).

### Implementer · Question

Event: `64f3d9c052e7ce47b2e70541e7363093` · 2026-10-03T02:11:20Z

> Blocking for d4's servers' case. init mints every child's /dev/cons through its one root badge at consoled, so all of them are charged to one bucket, and consoled's limits give a bucket state: 4 (servers/consoled/src/server.rs `limits`). So the 5th server after consoled cannot start: the image's manifest plus one test program refuses at boot with "boot-reader: could not mint a console connection for" (Refusal::Failed, i.e. a check that passed a boot that cannot run). Nothing in the check knows consoled's per-bucket state.
> Options:
> (a) [recommended] consoled's per-bucket state is MAX_THREADS (rt abi, 31; init starts at most MAX_THREADS - 1 servers by the watcher rule), stated with that why in `limits`' doc; BUDGET still holds (4 buckets: 4*(128K + 1K + 31*256) < 1 MiB; consoled's own `fits` check keeps refusing what does not). One host test: init's badge mints MAX_THREADS - 1 connections. consoled.md gains nothing but the reason line if you want it.
> (b) init checks the server count against a consoled constant it imports (couples init to consoled's crate) and refuses.
> (c) init mints a fresh root connection per child instead of through its own badge (each child its own bucket): but root badges are counted in the bucket rule and minted by the manifest, so this changes the bucket count rule.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `7bb6e53e081a0f39b8000cbf160a4efa` · 2026-10-03T02:11:30Z

> (a), with the pin made explicit: consoled's per-bucket state becomes MAX_THREADS, named not numbered, with the why in limits' doc (init starts at most MAX_THREADS - 1 servers, each minted a console through init's one root badge, so one bucket must hold them all); BUDGET recomputed in the same comment at the new state; consoled's fits check unchanged; the host test that init's badge mints MAX_THREADS - 1 connections. One sentence on consoled.md's sizing where the bucket state is stated, since a reader of the page would otherwise count 4. Not (b): a cross-crate constant for a limit the server owns. Not (c): it changes the bucket count rule the Architect ruled. Note that K16 raises MAX_THREADS to 255: the number follows by name, and the BUDGET comment must still hold at 255 - compute it for both and say so.
